title: Google ships Gemini 3.7 Flash three weeks after 3.6, cuts price in half
subtitle: The new workhorse model posts double-digit coding gains over its predecessor and lands at $0.75 per million input tokens through year-end.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Google released Gemini 3.7 Flash on August 13, three weeks after the 3.6 Flash release. The model keeps the 1-million-token context window, adds meaningful lifts on coding benchmarks — FrontierCode 1.1 Main climbs from 34.4 to 43.6, DeepSWE v1.1 from 49.0 to 65.3 — and Google says it beats comparable Anthropic and OpenAI models across nine tests. It is live now in Gemini Spark for AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in more than 160 countries.

The pricing is the interesting half. Introductory rates are $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens through December 31, 2026, half the launch price of 3.6 Flash. On January 1 the numbers double to $1.50 and $7.50. Google is aiming a workhorse tier squarely at the DeepSeek-shaped hole in the market — same class of intelligence as the frontier models, an order of magnitude cheaper per token — and betting that developers who wire it in during the discount window will keep it wired in at the higher price.

The release lands with Gemini 3.5 Pro still delayed. Google's cadence for the past two months has been Flash iterations shipping while Pro slips, which puts the workhorse tier in an odd position — better at coding than the last frontier release from the same lab, and available now, while the model that was supposed to hold the top of the stack is still in rework. It also arrives alongside a DeepMind leadership reshuffle Google announced last week.

Takeaway for learners: watch the price-per-token line, not the benchmark chart. A model that scores 5% higher on FrontierCode is a lab result; a model that costs half as much for the same accuracy changes what agents you can afford to run in a loop. The most useful skill right now is knowing which parts of your workflow are token-bound — long-horizon coding agents, batch document extraction, retrieval reranking — and being ready to swap the underlying model in a week when the price shifts.
